newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania vows to push ahead with economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania vows to push ahead with economic reforms.

text.p: Tanzania's vice-president told foreign investors on Tuesday his country would press ahead with economic reforms and strive to clear hurdles blocking development.
Vice-President Omar Ali Juma, in a speech read on behalf of President Benjamin Mkapa, vowed immediate action to streamline tax and investment policies and overhaul outdated immigration laws.
The speech won applause from more than 500 foreign investors, local businessmen and diplomats. Mkapa was attending a regional heads of government meeting in Nairobi on the crisis in Zaire.
More than 240 potential investment projects are earmarked for negotiation among some 300 foreign companies and 240 local entrepreneurs attending the four-day forum, Tanzania's first.

The head of the United Nations Development Fund in Tanzania, Victor Angelo, described the meeting as a "key milestone on the road to a more developed Tanzania", saying the country, one of the world's poorest, was a model of peace and stability in East Africa.
Tanzania embarked on economic reforms in 1986 and Mkapa said foreign investment, since 1993, totalled more than $2 billion, creating an estimated 128,000 jobs.
Under the reforms, Mkapa said, his country witnessed a return of monetary stability, improved terms of trade, reductions to the state payroll and ongoing parastatal sales.
Annual inflation, running at 40 per cent in 1993, now stands at 18 per cent and could be brought to a single digit level by 1997, he said.
Despite the good news Mkapa said his country still had a long way to go in the fight against red tape and bureaucracy, particularly in its tax policy, raising complaints from private investors.

He said he had ordered the establishment of a taskforce comprising members of the business community, the Tanzanian Revenue Authority (TRA) and treasury to review tax policy and incorporate the new proposals in the 1997/98 budget plan to boost investors confidence.
Mkapa pledged to ease procedures on the issuing of visas and work permits for foreigners.

"In this connection, I would like to assure potential investors and other visitors to Tanzania that the government this past week has taken measures to rationalise and ease these immigration formalities.

He said his government was fully committed to further economic reforms and maintaining macro-economic stability. He said his country had vast resources particularly in agriculture, mining and tourism which needed foreign capital for development.
